facts.claim: Town at the south-eastern end of the Bellarine Peninsula, on the entrance to Port Phillip, south of Swan Bay
Home to Fort Queenscliff and the terminus of the Bellarine Railway

name: Fort Queenscliff

facts.claim: Built from 1860 as an open battery on Shortland's Bluff to defend the entrance to Port Phillip
Headquarters of the chain of forts around Port Phillip Heads; manned as coastal defence 1883-1946
Fort enclosure and museum are visited by guided tour only, about 1.5 hours, starting from the fort gate
Tours run Saturday and Sunday at 11am and 1:45pm, none on public holidays; it is a defence area so bring ID

name: Bellarine Peninsula Railway

facts.claim: Volunteer-run steam tourist railway on a 16 km section of a former branch line between Queenscliff and Drysdale
The Swan Bay Express is a 45 minute train ride departing from Queenscliff Station
The Seaside Explorer runs the longer journey from Drysdale to the coast

name: Australian National Surfing Museum

facts.claim: Museum in Torquay widely cited as the world's largest surfing and beach culture museum
Includes the Australian Surfing Hall of Fame and surfboards from early wooden boards to modern designs
General admission is self-guided with no time limit

name: Split Point Lighthouse

facts.claim: Lighthouse at Aireys Inlet on the Great Ocean Road, on the Shipwreck Coast
Visitors can climb to the top for 360 degree coastal views, self-guided or on a tour
Known as the 'White Lady' of Round the Twist fame; dolphins or whales may be seen from the balcony

access_note: Children 5 and over only; weather permitting

Faces Bass Strait; coastal features include Point Danger and Zeally Bay
